task.description: Settle OQ-6 -- Lua 5.3 integer/float marshalling across VariableMerge and JSONB variable storage. Write lib/letflow/design/req150-lua-number-marshalling.md with empirical runs against the adopted tv-labs/lua runtime, a numbered normative rule REQ-159/REQ-160 can cite, the exact owning module/function, and the WASM-12 binding statement.
acceptance_criteria: lib/letflow/design/req150-lua-number-marshalling.md exists with a numbered normative section stating one rule per direction (Lua to Elixir, Elixir to Lua) that REQ-159 and REQ-160 can cite by section number

the artefact quotes real runs showing what an Elixir integer, an Elixir float, a Lua integer, and a Lua float each become on crossing the boundary in the adopted runtime -- observed, not inferred from the Lua 5.3 manual

the artefact states explicitly what happens to a float with no fractional part (e.g. 2.0) after a Jason.encode!/Jason.decode! round trip, with the real output quoted, since that is JSONB variable storage's actual behaviour
the artefact states the behaviour for an integer outside IEEE-754 exact range and for a JSON null, each with a defined outcome rather than 'undefined'
the artefact names the exact module and function that will own the conversion, so REQ-159 and REQ-160 share one implementation
the artefact states that WASM-12's parity requirement (REQ-171, REQ-172) binds the WASM half to this same rule, citing decision 0014's OQ-6
no file under lib/letflow/engine/ is modified by this requirement, confirmed by `git diff --stat` scoped to its commits

result.summary: Ran real code against tv-labs/lua 1.0.2 and a real disposable Postgres jsonb column (letflow_test99, dropped after use). Findings: Lua integer/float literals read back into Elixir as native integer()/float() with no wrapper; Elixir integer/float handed to Lua via Lua.set!/3 is seen via math.type as "integer"/"float" respectively, with NO collapse of a whole-number float (42.0 stays math.type "float"). Jason.encode!/decode! preserves the subtype because the decimal point is the wire-level carrier (3 -> "3" -> 3 integer; 3.0 -> "3.0" -> 3.0 float), confirmed again against a real jsonb column via Ecto.Adapters.SQL.query! (Postgrex's jsonb extension, the same path the plain :map field on instance_projections.variables uses). 2^53+1 round-trips byte-exact through Lua<->Elixir<->JSON<->real-jsonb since BEAM integers are arbitrary precision and Jason never routes an integer through a float. JSON null <-> Elixir nil <-> Lua nil round-trips symmetrically, confirmed by a script comparing host_nil == nil. Wrote lib/letflow/design/req150-lua-number-marshalling.md Sec 2 as the citable normative rule (2.1-2.6), naming Letflow.Engine.LuaNumberMarshalling.to_lua/1 and .from_lua/1 (not yet created -- both identity functions for the numeric/nil cases, deliberately explicit rather than omitted) as the shared owning module/function for REQ-159/REQ-160, and Sec 4 stating WASM-12 (REQ-171/REQ-172) binds to Sec 2 per decision 0014 OQ-6. git diff --stat confirms zero lib/letflow/engine/ changes.
